chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali ibn al-Zayyat, from Ubayd ibn Zurara, who said:

Ibn Qays al-Masir and Amr ibn Zarr entered upon Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), and I think Abu Hanifa was with them. Ibn Qays al-Masir spoke and said: 'We do not expel the people of our call and the people of our religion from faith due to sins and disobedience.'

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said to him: 'O Ibn Qays! As for the Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family), he said: The adulterer does not commit adultery while he is a believer, nor does the thief steal while he is a believer.'
So go, you and your companions, wherever you wish.
ai.seo_question: Do major sins expel a person from Islam according to Shia theology?
ai.summary: This hadith captures the pivotal theological debate between the Murji'ah, who held that faith (iman) is distinct from actions and thus major sins do not expel one from Islam, and the Shia Imams. Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) refutes this by citing the Prophet’s famous statement that the adulterer and thief are not believers *while committing* the act, establishing the Shia doctrine of 'Faith with Action' (Iman al-Amal). This distinction clarifies that while major sins are grave, they do not necessarily constitute disbelief (kufr) unless accompanied by denial, a key nuance in Shia kalām.

en.hubeali: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Ali Bin Al Zayyat, from Ubeyd Bin Zurara who said,

‘Ibn Qays Al-Masir and Amro Bin Zarr and I think with the two of them was Abu Haneefa, came over to Abu Ja’farasws. So Ibn Qays Al-Masir spoke and he said, ‘We do not expel the people of our calling, and the people of our religion from the Emān regarding the disobedience and the sins’.
So Abu Ja’farasws said to him: ‘O Ibn Qays! As for Rasool-Allahsaww, so hesaww said: ‘The adulterer would not commit adultery while he is a Momin, nor would the thief steal while he is a Momin’.
So you and your companions can go wherever you so desire to’.
en.sarwar: 22. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from Ali (ibn) al-Zayyat from ‘Ubayd ibn Zurara who has said the following: “

Once ibn Qays al-Masir and ‘Amr ibn Dharr - 1 think also abu Hanifah - came to see abu Ja’far, recipient of divine supreme covenant. Ibn Qays al-Masir spoke and said, ‘We do not expel people of our own mission and people of our own nation from belief just because of disobedience and sin.’
Abu Ja’far (a.s.) said, ‘O ibn Qays, the Messenger of Allah has said, ‘One does not fornicate while he is a believer, and one does not steal while he is a believer.’
You and your people may go wherever you wish.’”
